statement: The repository shall keep one machine-wide model registry and one machine-wide lock: models/registry.yaml holds intent (role to family, plus effort, with roles named by use such as primary, extractor, rater, adjudicator, teacher, judge and background), and models/models.lock.yaml holds the resolved model id per family, the CLI version that resolved it, the date and the evidence file. The command `seldon models show` shall print both files, and the Python accessor `seldon.models.resolve(role)` shall be the only way any code on the machine obtains a model id.

When `seldon models refresh` runs, it shall resolve "latest in family" using Anthropic's own resolver, the newest Claude Code CLI, by installing the newest Claude Code into a versioned prefix with `npm install --prefix` and never the global install, running one minimal `-p --model <alias> --output-format json` call per family and recording the `modelUsage` model id, writing the lock, appending a `models_lock_bumped` event naming the old and new ids, and committing. The refresh shall cost four short calls, shall run when a task is authored and when a run starts, and its result shall be cached for the day.

Every launcher (the seldon dispatcher, squiddy `model_client` and extraction daemon, the ai-readiness-kg and arnold harnesses, and any other model call site the inventory finds) shall set the lock's ids into `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL` and `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` so that CLI background work follows the lock, pass `--model <id>` for its role, and exec the CLI version the lock names, never launching from an alias.

If a config value is a model alias or a model id, then the config shall fail conformance, because a config value shall name a registry role instead; desktop sessions and memory shall carry no model ids, and a task file's `**Model:**` header shall name a role.

If a task's `**Model:**` header, or a `--model` argument in one of its code blocks, names an id not in the current lock, then `seldon cc register` and dispatcher candidacy shall refuse the task and quote the lock in the refusal; prose that cites history is not checked.

The system shall record, for each launched call, the requested model id and the served model id from `modelUsage`; if the served id does not match the requested id, then the system shall stop the unit with the named failure `model_substituted`. The system shall set `switchModelsOnFlag: false` in launched processes, so that a classifier flag becomes a recorded refusal and never a silent model switch.

While a run is in flight, the system shall keep the run's lock entry until the run ends. When a version bump occurs, the system shall re-pilot each gated or sealed instrument, per H-006 R-30. The system shall keep the ids that sealed records were made with, treating them as history and not as staleness.

The project does not deploy managed settings (an `availableModels` allowlist or denial of superseded models), because an allowlist would also bind the operator's interactive sessions and denying superseded models would also disable classifier fallback targets; ordering is instead enforced by R3 to R6 where calls are made, with the receipt as proof, and this decision is to be revisited if a call site is found that R3 cannot reach.

Every new design note shall carry a `## Prior art` section with two subsections, `### External` and `### Internal`, in which each entry is a receipt: a library receipt names the query string, the index release and its sha256, and one or more returned row ids; an internal receipt names the query string, the repository and its commit sha, and file:line hits; a web receipt names the URL and the retrieval date and is allowed only in External, and an External section containing only web receipts shall also carry at least one library query, even one that found nothing; a finding of "no prior art" shall be recorded as a receipt of the query that found nothing and never as a sentence.

When `seldon prior-art verify <note>` is run, the seldon tool shall re-run each library query against the named release and each internal query against the named commit, and shall pass a receipt only when the cited ids or lines are in the result. If a named release or commit is no longer loadable, then the tool shall fail that receipt with `release_unavailable`, naming the release or commit. The tool shall record the verification once, at commit (R4), so that a later library rebuild does not orphan an accepted note.

The `seldon prior-art search --internal "<query>"` command shall, until governed graphs cover the sibling repositories, search at each repository's HEAD `docs/design`, `docs/research`, `docs/decisions`, `CLAUDE.md`, `DECISIONS_INHERITED.md` and `handoffs`, in every repository listed under a new `prior_art.internal_roots` key (seeded with seldon, squiddy, ai-readiness-kg, arnold, icsp_notebook, the `~/.wintermute/docs` tree, and the workbench audit folder), print receipts in R1's form, append the query, the commits and the hits to `state/prior_art_queries.jsonl`, and match lexically (ripgrep, case-insensitive, all terms within one paragraph) as a search and not an admission test, so DI-075 does not bar it, with R5 measuring its recall. The `seldon prior-art search --library "<query>"` command shall wrap squiddy-library `search` in-process and log the same way, and both commands shall be exposed as one MCP tool, `seldon_prior_art_search`, so Desktop design sessions use them. When governed graphs cover the sibling repositories (AD-031-R1, Issue `25da4d06`), a governed-graph arm shall be added beside the lexical arm and shall not substitute for it, since the lexical arm is the recall control's baseline.

The gate shall refuse at two points: when `seldon verify` (pre-commit) sees a commit that adds a design note under `docs/design/` whose prior-art section is missing, has an empty subsection, or fails R2, it shall refuse the commit and write the verdict to the governed ledger beside the note's hash; when `seldon cc register` is given a task whose governing note has no passing verdict, it shall refuse the registration. Design notes on main at the merge commit of AD-036 are baseline, shall be listed and grandfathered, and shall not be re-litigated. Each refusal shall quote the missing part and name AD-036.

The internal search tool shall be subject to a pre-registered recall control whose positive set is the 18 known-relevant locations (the 14 file:line entries of G5 problem 1's timeline plus the four ai-readiness-kg §1 and §7 lines cited in section 2), queried with one query per entry that is fixed before the run and written from the entry's topic, never from its wording; the tool passes when the Wilson-95 lower bound of recall at top 20 is at or above 0.70, and the control shall be re-run on every change to the tool. If the tool fails the control, then the failure shall be reported with the misses, shall not block R4 (because the gate checks presence and verifiability, not search quality), and shall open a design task for the governed-graph arm.

The gate shall verify only that a search happened and that the hits it cites exist, and it shall not be relied on to establish that the author read, weighed or used the hits; quality remains with review (AD-020 multi-lens) and with the operator.

When the prior-art tool lands, the `seldon prior-art verify docs/design/AD-036_prior_art_receipts_gate.md` command shall pass on the AD-036 note, the prose of the note's internal section shall be converted into receipts by re-running each internal search with the tool and recording the results in an addendum, never by editing the AD-036 note file, and AD-035 shall be checked the same way with its result recorded in an AD-035 addendum.

The system shall treat effort as a declared input, as the model id is: `models/registry.yaml` shall refuse `effort: default` and name an effort level for each role, set to the documented default effort of the model the lock now serves (`medium` for opus, sonnet and haiku; `high` for fable) except that `document_extractor` and `demand_judge` stay `high` as measured; launchers shall pass `--effort`, receipts shall record it, and a lock bump shall record any change in a family's documented default effort.

Any test that can reach a model launcher without a fake shall run only under an explicit opt-in variable named in its skip reason, in every repository MODEL-001 touched, and a PATH shim that records invocations shall prove zero model calls by default.
